sections.h2: Can a Dunedin house sell quickly for cash?
sections.html:
Yes. With no loan approval and no lender appraisal in the way, a Dunedin sale can close as fast as the title search and payoff letters permit. What actually slows sales is the house: repairs, a tenant, an estate or a lender's deadline. Selling directly also spares you an inspection-driven repair list to argue over.

Dunedin is on the Gulf side of Pinellas County, north of Clearwater and St. Petersburg, and has more than 35,000 residents. It is a walkable town with a Scottish name and Scottish street names, which draws buyers who want to live near downtown, second-home owners and investors. A cash buyer can serve any of them without asking you to stage anything.

sections.h2: Homestead in Pinellas County after a sale
sections.html:
The Pinellas County Property Appraiser prints the homestead benefit as $51,411 off assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to every tax on the bill. The remaining $26,411 covers value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves out school taxes.

That exemption ends when you sell. A sale, renting the property, any change of ownership or moving out all stop it. If the buyer closes after January 1, your homestead may still appear on the August notice, and the credit comes off on December 31. The buyer then files an original application by March 1 to start their own.

The assessment cap does not follow the house either. The next January the state resets the assessment to full market level. If you are buying elsewhere in Florida, ask about portability, which carries part of your capped benefit to a new homestead established within three years.

sections.h2: Fixed costs of a Dunedin sale
sections.html:
The state and county charges are set by law, so you can see them before you list. The largest is usually the deed stamp tax, 70 cents for every $100 paid, which applies in every county except Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable for it, although the contract normally lands it on the seller.

The Pinellas clerk also bills a per-page recording fee under section 28.24, with technology and trust fund add-ons. Ask the clerk for the total on your particular instrument.

sections.h2: What a new owner brings to file for homestead
sections.html:
The appraiser's office wants proof of residency for every owner, spouses included. That means a Florida driver license and auto registration, a voter card or permanent resident card where one applies, and Social Security numbers for all owners and spouses, even when only one spouse is on the deed.

An owner who holds a residency-based exemption elsewhere will be denied. The office asks for proof that the other exemption was removed, or the latest tax bill on any property owned elsewhere, within 30 days of applying.

  • File online or in person at one of the appraiser's offices.
  • Owners who had homestead last year and still live there get a receipt in early January.
  • Tell the office if you stop qualifying, for example after renting the home out.

Pass this list to your buyer. A quick, correct filing keeps their first tax bill predictable.

A Florida deed must be in writing and witnessed by two people, and section 689.01 allows witnessing over audio-video technology. The closing agent normally drafts the deed and takes it to the clerk. The usual order:

  1. Sign the sales contract and open a title order.
  2. Clear liens, loan payoffs and any open permits the search turns up.
  3. Sign the deed before two witnesses.
  4. Pay stamps and recording fees to the clerk.
  5. Let the appraiser update the tax roll afterward.

Estate sales differ. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is untaxed, while quitclaims and deeds given to a lender do carry stamp tax.

Act before the legal clock runs out. Tax bills arrive in November with a 4 percent discount that falls to 1 percent by February. Unpaid taxes are late from April 1, and certificates on them go to auction by June 1.

Foreclosure moves through the courts. Once final judgment is entered, the clerk sets a public sale 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff consents to a delay, and the winning bidder puts down 5 percent. Selling first can retire the loan and leave any equity with you. After a sale has already happened, the clerk can explain how surplus funds are claimed.

  • Ask the Pinellas Tax Collector about installment and deferral options.
  • Get your lender's payoff figure in writing.
  • Speak with the clerk about surplus after an auction.

Compare what lands in your account, not the headline price. A listing may reach a higher number, but it adds showings, repair negotiations, financing risk and months of carrying costs. A cash purchase moves fast and the buyer accepts the house as is.

Run the closing statement for each route: loan payoff, stamps, recording, unpaid taxes and the repairs you would otherwise fund. For recent nearby sales, search the Pinellas Property Appraiser's public records or ask a local agent. Written terms from every buyer make the comparison honest, and a request for fees from you before closing is a reason to stop and talk to an attorney.

sections.h2: If a tenant lives in the house
sections.html: A tenant does not block a sale. The lease still binds both sides, and Florida sets minimum notice periods for ending a tenancy, so read the lease before you promise a buyer an empty house. Tell each buyer about the tenancy at the start, and keep the lease, rent history and deposit records together for the title company.

sections.h2: Getting ready before you accept an offer
sections.html:
A few errands done in advance keep a direct sale from stalling. Locate your recorded deed and legal description. Ask your lender for a written payoff. Gather permit records for any repairs, and settle or at least disclose open permits. Pull the latest tax bill from the Pinellas Tax Collector. If the house is rented, find the lease and deposit records. When an estate is involved, work out early who has authority to sign, because a title company will insist on seeing it.

With those items in hand you can answer a buyer's questions in a day, which matters when the whole appeal of a cash sale is speed. Afterward, remember to cancel insurance and move utilities only once the deed has recorded, so the house is never uncovered mid-sale.

faqs.q: Who pays deed stamps on a Dunedin sale?
faqs.a: The contract usually puts it on the seller, though the state makes every party to the deed liable. The clerk collects the flat 70 cents for every $100 paid.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. It ends with the sale. The new owner files with the Pinellas appraiser by March 1, and any leftover credit on a notice comes off December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant living in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease still binds the parties, and Florida sets minimum notice periods for ending a tenancy, so read the lease first.

faqs.q: What happens to my Save Our Homes savings?
faqs.a: The buyer does not get them, because the assessment resets to full market level the next January. You may move your own benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability.
The Pinellas clerk's recording office, and the closing agent usually files it.
